sa: अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः।
स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ॥
tr: anāśritaḥ karmaphalaṃ kāryaṃ karma karoti yaḥ
sa saṃnyāsī ca yogī ca na niragnirna cākriyaḥ
en: Whoever does the work that is to be done without depending on its fruit is a renunciate and a yogi; not the one who merely gives up the sacred fire, or all activity.
speaker: Krishna said

sa: यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव।
tr: yaṃ saṃnyāsamiti prāhuryogaṃ taṃ viddhi pāṇḍava
en: What they call renunciation, know that to be yoga, Pandava; for no one becomes a yogi without renouncing selfish intention.
For the sage who wishes to climb to yoga, action is said to be the means; for the one who has climbed it, calm is said to be the means.
When one is attached neither to sense objects nor to actions, and has renounced all selfish intention, one is said to have climbed to yoga.
Lift yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is its enemy.
The self is a friend to one who has conquered oneself by oneself; but for one who has not, the self turns hostile, like an enemy.
For one who has conquered the self and is at peace, the supreme Self stays steady, in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour.
Satisfied with knowledge and its realisation, unshakable, senses conquered, the yogi to whom a clod, a stone and gold are the same is called disciplined.
Excellent is the one who is even-minded toward well-wishers, friends, enemies, the indifferent, the neutral, the hateful and relatives, toward the good and the wicked alike.
The yogi should keep concentrating the mind, staying in seclusion, alone, with mind and body controlled, free from hope and from possessiveness.
In a clean place, setting up a firm seat for oneself, neither too high nor too low, covered with kusha grass, a deerskin and a cloth,
sitting there, making the mind one-pointed, controlling the workings of thought and sense, one should practise yoga to purify the self.
Holding body, head and neck erect and still, steady, gazing at the tip of one's nose and not looking around,

sa: मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः ॥
tr: manaḥ saṃyamya maccitto yukta āsīta matparaḥ
en: serene, fearless, firm in the vow of celibacy, the mind restrained and thinking of me, one should sit disciplined, intent on me.
Always practising in this way, mind controlled, the yogi reaches the peace that rests in me, the supreme nirvana.
Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who does not eat at all; not for one who sleeps too much, nor for one who stays awake too long, Arjuna.
For one moderate in food and recreation, measured in action, moderate in sleep and waking, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.
When the disciplined mind rests in the Self alone, free from longing for any desire, one is called united in yoga.

sa: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता।
tr: yathā dīpo nivātastho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā
en: "As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker": that is the image for the yogi of controlled mind, practising union with the Self.
Where the mind, restrained by the practice of yoga, comes to rest; where, seeing the Self by the self, one is content in the Self;

sa: वेत्ति यत्र न चैवायं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः ॥
tr: vetti yatra na caivāyaṃ sthitaścalati tattvataḥ
en: where one knows that boundless happiness, grasped by the intellect and beyond the senses, and, established there, never moves from the truth;

sa: यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः।
tr: yaṃ labdhvā cāparaṃ lābhaṃ manyate nādhikaṃ tataḥ
en: having gained which, one thinks no other gain greater; established in which, one is not shaken even by heavy sorrow;
know that to be yoga: the breaking of the bond with sorrow. This yoga should be practised with determination and an undiscouraged mind.
Giving up completely all desires born of selfish intention, restraining the whole crowd of senses on every side with the mind,

sa: आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥
tr: ātmasaṃsthaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā na kiñcidapi cintayet
en: little by little one should come to rest, the intellect held firm; making the mind abide in the Self, one should think of nothing else.
Wherever the restless, unsteady mind wanders off, from there one should draw it back and bring it under the control of the Self alone.
Supreme happiness comes to the yogi whose mind is at peace, whose passion is calmed, who is free of impurity and has become one with Brahman.
Always practising in this way, free from impurity, the yogi easily enjoys the boundless happiness of contact with Brahman.
With the self disciplined by yoga, seeing the same everywhere, one sees the Self in all beings and all beings in the Self.

sa: यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति।
तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥
tr: yo māṃ paśyati sarvatra sarvaṃ ca mayi paśyati
tasyāhaṃ na praṇaśyāmi sa ca me na praṇaśyati
en: Whoever sees me everywhere and sees everything in me, I am never lost to them, and they are never lost to me.

sa: सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते ॥
tr: sarvathā vartamāno'pi sa yogī mayi vartate
en: Whoever, established in oneness, worships me as dwelling in all beings, that yogi lives in me, however they live.

sa: सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं सः योगी परमो मतः ॥
tr: sukhaṃ vā yadi vā duḥkhaṃ saḥ yogī paramo mataḥ
en: Whoever, by comparison with oneself, sees the same in everything, Arjuna, whether pleasure or pain, is considered the highest yogi.

sa: एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥
tr: etasyāhaṃ na paśyāmi cañcalatvāt sthitiṃ sthirām
en: This yoga of evenness that you have taught, Madhusudana: I cannot see how it can last, because the mind is so restless.
speaker: Arjuna said

sa: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्।
tr: cañcalaṃ hi manaḥ kṛṣṇa pramāthi balavaddṛḍham
en: The mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, strong and stubborn. Controlling it seems to me as hard as controlling the wind.

sa: अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥
tr: abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇa ca gṛhyate
en: No doubt, mighty-armed, the mind is restless and hard to restrain. But by practice (abhyasa) and detachment (vairagya), son of Kunti, it can be held.
speaker: Krishna said

sa: असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः।
tr: asaṃyatātmanā yogo duṣprāpa iti me matiḥ
en: Yoga is hard to reach for one who is not self-controlled, I agree. But one who is self-controlled and keeps striving can reach it by the right means.

sa: अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥
tr: aprāpya yogasaṃsiddhiṃ kāṃ gatiṃ kṛṣṇa gacchati
en: What becomes of one who has faith but does not strive enough, whose mind wanders from yoga, and who fails to reach its perfection, Krishna?
speaker: Arjuna said

en: Fallen from both, does such a one not perish like a torn cloud, mighty-armed, without support, lost on the path to Brahman?
Please cut away this doubt of mine completely, Krishna; no one but you can dispel it.
Partha, there is no destruction for such a one, neither here nor hereafter. No one who does good, my friend, ever comes to a bad end.
speaker: Krishna said

en: Having reached the worlds of the righteous and lived there for countless years, the one who fell from yoga is born in the home of the pure and prosperous.
Or they are born into a family of wise yogis, though a birth like that is harder to find in this world.

sa: यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन ॥
tr: yatate ca tato bhūyaḥ saṃsiddhau kurunandana
en: There they regain the understanding of their former life, and from there they strive again for perfection, joy of the Kurus.
By that earlier practice they are carried along, even without wanting to. Even one who only wishes to know yoga goes beyond the ritual of the Vedas.
But the yogi who strives with effort, cleansed of impurities and perfected over many births, then reaches the highest goal.
The yogi is greater than the ascetics, greater even than the learned, greater than those who perform ritual works. So be a yogi, Arjuna.

sa: श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मां स मे युक्ततमो मतः ॥
tr: śraddhāvānbhajate yo māṃ sa me yuktatamo mataḥ
en: And of all yogis, the one who worships me with faith, their inner self absorbed in me, I consider the most united with me.
